questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to go on exchange to a place where I would feel welcomed and get to see what I think is one of the best parts of the USA.
I am a US citizen, so I wanted to connect with that part of myself.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Berkeley is a great place with very nice people! I had some great lectures there, who I connected with on a personal level. I can recommend

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, but I could have had more information about the first coming days. So make sure to download the golden bears/cal bears app.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an orientation week, which thoroughly enjoyed. We were shown the campus and its facilities including services such as CAPS - the university's own mental health service.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was a bit of a challenge, but not too difficult. I recommend staying in the coops (Berkeley Student Cooperative), where the rent is by far the cheapest.
If you live at the larger houses such as the one I lived at (Cloyne, CZ), then there will be food every day in the form mostly of dinner. Furthermore, the house will have lots of groceries, and I by lots I mean A LOT, that you are free to take as a resident of the house. Cloyne is substance free, so you cant drink beer, but I found that was great for me, as I got a lot of social relationships without drinking, and when I wanted to drink I just went out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: South side is considered a little more dangerous, but none of those people I got to know was involved in any dangerous incidents. As long as you don't wear headphones at night whilst walking down alone you are probably good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The overall market for housing isn't great, but the student cooperative is a highly valuable experience for most people.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought it was pretty easy. They have a great course planner, look out for DeCal's I have heard that they are fun!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You go onto their registration service through CalCentral, and hereafter it is pretty straightforward. The registration opens sometime in mid july

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot, since our counselor was in the process of switching jobs. But otherwise they would hold workshops and an introduction meeting for the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very succesful, but I recommend people signing up for more courses than they need, because you can drop any course before the first of September.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register early, look up rate my professor ratings, choose young over old professors, attend more classes first week to see if you would like to drop one course and take another.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Teachers were great, but classes were hard and required a lot more discipline than what I have been used to.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took an analytic mechanics course, which by far is the hardest course I have ever taken. The other courses were of fine level, but required a lot of homework still.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Shorter sessions, which was very enjoyable.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Analytic Mechanics, Experimental courses in Mathematics (problem solving course in math and a great course), Introduction to Number Theory (enjoyable) and Berkeley Connect.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Experimental Courses in Mathematics. You show up for class having solved or tried to solve the homework problems, and then you work them through together on the blackboard in a session lasting 1.5 hours.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. Just as a note to people, if you don't have food as I did through my house, then food and housing costs will be far more expensive. Also my housing cost was 4133 dollars for a semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied, I played on two soccer teams, which I enjoyed a lot.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: IM Sports, Football games and a whole lot of clubs (chess club, dance club and so on)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ISAB is a great club to meet other international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Muir woods, Alcatraz, Lake Tahoe, Yosemite and walking around san fransisco.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, but be aware that you have to adapt to their social norms. In Denmark we a more joking, and joke about a lot of things, that people there might not like.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live in a coop, join a club either IM sports or when they table.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the people. You can join almost any group of people and they will be open and welcoming towards you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Sign up for the coops, select some good courses, be diligent with your studies so you can use the rest of the time on other things (do homework before partying).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Do not expect Berkeley to be a huge party city, but there are parties if you find the right places (Raleighs, Kips, Monroe(SF)).
Mexican food and Indian food are in my opinion the way to go..

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Integrating with people at my house, getting to know a bunch of great people. Furthermore, I got quite close to some of my fellow danish exchange students, because we lived together in a big coop. In addition I got super close to a professor, and enjoyed going to office hours and clubs.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being studious enough. I was often late on assignments, but I think this might just be a me problem. Dont study hard, but study smart. Begin your assignments on the day.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
